You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 Coal Baron Coal Baron – or Glück Auf in German, after a greeting German miners use when wishing one another luck – has players sending miners underground to dig tunnels and acquire coal, which comes in four levels of quality and is used to fulfill contracts. The game lasts three rounds, and in each round players take turns placing their workers on action spaces; you can place on a space occupied by another player, but you need to place additional workers in order to do so. Each player has an individual elevator shaft, and will need to use workers to extract coal and bring it to the surface, while also competing for contracts and scrounging for cash in order to do everything else that needs to be done! Number of players: 2 - 4 Game duration: 46 mn Complexity: 2 / 5 Play Coal Baron and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Setup 3 Shifts 4 Turn 5 Action Spaces 6 Scoring 6.1 Lorry 6.2 Mining 6.3 Delivery 6.4 Money 6.5 Order 6.6 Bank 6.7 End of Shift 6.8 Game End Overview Mine for coals, complete and dispatch the most contracts over three shifts. Setup As part of setup, each player will pick 3 Order cards, each card taken one at a time in turn order Shifts Each shift comprises of placing workers. Turn Place a worker on your chosen action space. If there is already a man/men there, one extra man must be used. Two men replace one man, three men replace two men etc. Workers that got replaced wait for the next shift in the Canteen. Once you have run out of workers, you are skipped until the other players have all completed the Shift. Action Spaces There are 8 types of Spaces (+the Canteen, which can't be accessed voluntarily) Lorry - [wagons or carts in English nations] Lorries do not refill - choose which lorries you need to buy to fulfil your chosen contracts. Mining - Claim 6 or 10 movement spaces then lower your cart down to the appropriate level. Load your coals, raise your cart and load the coals onto your contract cards. Delivery - When your contracts are complete, they can be shipped off via the delivery space with the correct icon. Money - You only need money to buy the loaded lorries/wagons. Everything else is paid for with man hours. Order - Choose which contracts you want to complete, to earn the stated points. Finance - Withdraw money to pay for the lorries/carts. Bank - Not needed men can go to the bank, where they'll receive $1. Re-ordering - If the lorry/cart you want isn't available, you may get it by rearranging the next five cards of the draw pile. Same with the contract cards. Scoring Scoring takes place at the end of each shift. You will earn the points on your delivered contract cards Additional points - Delivering the most coals in each of the colours, delivering the most coals in each of the delivery types, the most empty lorries in each of the colours. [Lorries containing coals are not counted] You will lose a point for uncompleted contracts and 2pts for each unbalanced minecart. [This is the difference between your purchased lit lorry/carts and your purchased unlit lorry/carts. Left over money is the tie breaker. Lorry Gain the depicted Tunnel Tile by paying the cost in Marks per Lorry and type of Lorry Yellow Lorry costs 1 (2 if two) Brown Lorry costs 2 (4 if two) Grey Lorry costs 3 (6 if two) Black Lorry costs 4 (8 if two) After you've paid for it, each Lorry depicted gains 1 Coal of its same colour Then it is added to the Pit on its colour level as well as the correct side (Left side has Lanterns in the ceiling, right does not) Points may be lost if your lighted mine and your unlighted mine become too imbalanced. [Rating: 2/10] Point salad.  Everybody scores!  Winner determined less by strategy than by whether other players are going for similar objectives as you thus diluting your score.

[Rating: 2/10] Never played.  Looked like interesting game but theme and mechanics were turnoff for partner.  Sent to game cafe

[Rating: 2/10] Best part is the fundamental worker placement mechanism: spots initially require one worker. Then, if you want to go to a space that already has a worker, you must place two workers. Or if the space has two workers, place three workers, etc. It's simple but effective and forces you to weigh and constantly re-weigh the effective "value" of your remaining workers and decide whether you want to spend several of them on the action you [i]really[/i] want or take a suboptimal action thereby spending fewer workers. [Rating: 3/10] Very dry game, and it's super annoying how the majorities (there are 12 things in which you score majorities) can be swinged by just one. No engine building.

[Rating: 3/10] Pretty much as boring as they could possibly make it. An antiquated design from designers whose best days are past them. They were great in their day, but this is not their day.

[Rating: 3/10] Points de victoire incompréhensibles! Heureusement les parties sont courtes. Il faut vraiment aimer ce style de jeu...

[Rating: 3/10] 1 Play  Felt like a diceless Stone age. Is an alright game. Otys does so many similar things better. Art and aethetics are kinda horrible.

[Rating: 4/10] The design is solid, but it is just uninspiring. The theme is blah (probably ruined by Magnum Sal) and the mechanics do not set it apart in any  meaningful way. I would be happy to play again, but don't see my opinion changing at all.

[Rating: 4/10] Not the most exciting game ever. Action Points meets Worker Placement. There's some interest and tension in timing your actions to avoid being blocked by others while simultaneously getting in their way. It's a game where players with good memories can use that to their advantage, tracking who is winning which scoring categories and by how much. Presumably the memory element is there to speed the game up and stop players being quite so analytical.

[Rating: 4/10] Good, but unremarkable, worker placement game.  Had it come out in the mid to late 00's it might have been great, but today it is just retreading ground laid by games before it.  I would not choose to play it over Stone Age, Caylus, or even Lords of Waterdeep, so I won't be keeping it.    The components are of poor quality, and frankly, R&R should be ashamed.  The tiles are thin and warped.  The paper money is all the same size and color regardless of denomination.  It feels like you are playing a prototype, or maybe a $25 FFG Silver Line game - certainly not a $45 production piece.
